sections.overview: The short worm lizard is an amphisbaenian reptile in the family Trogonophidae. It is the only recognized species of Pachycalamus and is known from Socotra, Yemen.
sections.identification: It is the type species of the genus Pachycalamus. The accessible species account does not provide enough diagnostic detail for a reliable field description, so identification should rely on specialist keys or specimens.
sections.habitat: The type locality and verified distribution are on Socotra Island in the Socotra Archipelago. Available species accounts provide little information on its microhabitat, so a more precise habitat preference cannot be stated confidently.
sections.diet: No dependable account of prey or feeding ecology was located. Its diet should not be inferred from the better-studied worm lizards alone.
sections.behavior: The sources consulted do not provide a detailed activity pattern or direct behavioral observations for this species.
sections.reproduction: The Reptile Database records it as oviparous. Clutch size, nest site and development are not established in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: Pachycalamus brevis is part of Socotra's endemic terrestrial reptile fauna. Archipelago surveys include it among the recorded land reptiles, but its abundance, diet and interactions remain poorly documented.
sections.conservation: The last located IUCN assessment (2011) classified it as Data Deficient. This means information was insufficient to assess risk, not that the species is safe; reassessment would be useful.
